title: Pulley and Mass System (part 3)
source: neb-class-11-physics — Pulley and Mass System, pages 89-95 [neb-class-11-physics-book.pdf]
textbookText: Introduction: Observe the following phenomena: i) You can easily walk along the pitched road while you find it hard to walk along a muddy way. ii) You easily write it down on paper but it feels difficult on a piece of plastic. iii) You can easily hold a nut on a wall. iv) A moving fan finally stops after the electric switch is off, disobeying Newton’s first law. v) A rolling ball on a ground finally stops disobeying the first law. Considering the events occurring above, there is some phenomenon in each activity that opposes our motion called friction. The phenomenon of arising an opposing force against the motion between two solids in touch is called friction. The force on the friction is called frictional force. vi) It acts against the motion. vii) It opposes the relative motion between the solids.
